title: Impressions: Definition
measures: Defines an impression as each time an ad is shown on Google or the Google Network; notes that sometimes only part of an ad is shown (for example in Google Maps).
limitations: Glossary page; Google may change it without notice. Google Ads definition only, not Search Console or Business Profile impressions.

title: Click: Definition
measures: Defines an ad click; states a click is counted even if the person does not reach the website, so clicks and website visits can differ; invalid clicks are filtered and not charged.
limitations: Glossary page; Google may change it without notice.

title: Clickthrough rate (CTR): Definition
measures: CTR = clicks divided by impressions; notes that a good CTR is relative to what is advertised and on which networks.
limitations: Glossary page; gives no benchmark values.

title: Average cost-per-click (Avg. CPC): Definition
measures: Average CPC = total cost of clicks divided by total clicks; based on actual CPC and can differ from max. CPC.
limitations: Glossary page; gives no benchmark values.

title: Conversion rate: Definition
measures: Conversion rate = conversions divided by ad interactions that can be tracked to a conversion in the same period; can exceed 100% when several conversion actions or 'Every' counting are used.
limitations: Glossary page; describes Google Ads reporting only.

title: Key event, Conversion & Purchase definition
measures: Defines a key event (an action the advertiser has defined as valuable) and a conversion (an action used to measure ad performance and optimize bidding, eligible for bidding and reporting in Google Ads).
limitations: Glossary page; terminology changed in 2024 and may change again.

title: About Target ROAS bidding
measures: Describes ROAS as conversion value per cost (average conversion value, for example revenue, per dollar spent on ads) and how Target ROAS bidding uses reported conversion values.
limitations: Bidding-strategy article; ROAS here uses whatever conversion value the advertiser reports, which may not be collected revenue. Notes naming changes from June 2026.

title: About access levels in your Google Ads account
measures: Lists Google Ads access levels (Email-only, Billing, Read-only, Standard, Admin) and what each can do; notes the risk of having only one administrator and that admins of an owning manager account can edit user access.
limitations: Product documentation; access levels may change.

title: About Analytics sessions
measures: Defines a GA4 session (a period of user interaction; times out after 30 minutes of inactivity by default); session counts are estimated; session attribution carries gclid, UTM parameters and referrer.
limitations: Product documentation for GA4 only.

title: [GA4] Analytics dimensions and metrics
measures: Reference definitions, including engaged sessions (10 seconds or longer, 1+ key events or 2+ page/screen views) and engagement rate = engaged sessions / total sessions.
limitations: Long reference list; definitions are GA4-specific.

title: Mark events as key events
measures: How events are marked as key events in GA4; marking affects reports from the time of creation and does not change historic data.
limitations: Product documentation; limits and default key events may change.

title: Add, edit, and delete Analytics users and user groups
measures: Users are added at account or property level; Administrator role is needed to add, modify or delete users.
limitations: Product documentation.

title: URL builders: Collect campaign data with custom URLs
measures: Lists UTM parameters (utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign and others) and recommends always using source, medium and campaign.
limitations: Product documentation.

title: Understand your Business Profile performance & insights
measures: Defines Business Profile performance metrics: interactions, searches, views (unique viewers, once per day), directions, calls (clicks on the call button), website clicks, messages, bookings. Data includes organic and Google Ads; only for verified profiles.
limitations: Only metrics that apply to a business appear; definitions may change.

title: Guidelines for representing your business on Google
measures: Eligibility and naming rules for Business Profiles: name should reflect the real-world business name; no keywords in address lines; separate guidance for individual practitioners.
limitations: Policy page; Google may change it without notice.

title: Understand factors that determine local ranking
measures: Local results are mainly based on relevance, distance and prominence; there is no way to request or pay for better local ranking.
limitations: High-level description; Google does not disclose algorithm details.

title: Add or remove Business Profile owners & managers
measures: Owner vs manager roles: a profile can have multiple owners but one primary owner; managers cannot add or remove users or remove the profile; each user needs their own Google Account.
limitations: Product documentation.

title: Mobile site and mobile-first indexing best practices
measures: Google uses the mobile version of a site's content for indexing and ranking; content parity between mobile and desktop is expected.
limitations: Page last updated 2025-12-10 per its footer.

title: URL Inspection tool
measures: The URL Inspection tool shows Google's indexed version of a page and can test whether a live URL might be indexable.
limitations: Requires Search Console access to the property.

title: Web Vitals
measures: Core Web Vitals good thresholds: LCP within 2.5 seconds, INP of 200 milliseconds or less, CLS of 0.1 or less, measured at the 75th percentile of page loads, segmented by mobile and desktop. INP became a stable Core Web Vital in 2024; lab tools cannot measure INP (TBT is a lab proxy).
limitations: Last updated 2024-10-31 per the page; thresholds may be revised.

title: Introduction to Lighthouse
measures: Lighthouse is an open-source automated tool with audits for performance, accessibility, SEO and more.
limitations: Lab tool; automated accessibility checks do not cover every WCAG criterion. Last updated 2025-06-02 per the page.

title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
measures: WCAG 2.2 success criteria, including 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) 4.5:1, 2.4.7 Focus Visible, 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum), 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) 24 by 24 CSS pixels, 3.2.6 Consistent Help, 3.3.7 Redundant Entry, 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum).
limitations: Technical standard; conformance requires checking every applicable criterion, not a sample.

title: 16 CFR Part 465 — Use of Consumer Reviews and Testimonials
measures: FTC rule text: prohibits fake or false reviews, buying reviews of a particular sentiment, undisclosed insider reviews, company-controlled review sites and certain review suppression.
limitations: Regulation text retrieved through the eCFR API (title 16 up to date as of 2026-11-05); not legal advice. State laws may add obligations.
